plain.text: When the uproar ended, Paul encouraged the disciples, said goodbye and set out for Macedonia and then Greece, where he stayed three months. Because of a plot against him, he went back through Macedonia. Several companions travelled with him from different churches. They met again at Troas.

On the first day of the week, they came together to break bread. Paul talked until midnight, since he planned to leave the next day. A young man named Eutychus, sitting in a window, sank into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on, and fell from the third storey. He was picked up dead. Paul went down, threw himself on him and put his arms around him. "Don't be alarmed," he said. "He's alive!" Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, ate, and talked until daylight. The people took the young man home alive and were greatly comforted.
Paul and his companions travelled along the coast. Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, hurrying to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost.

From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church. He reminded them how he had served the Lord with humility and tears, teaching them publicly and from house to house, telling everyone to turn to God in repentance and have faith in the Lord Jesus. Now, compelled by the Spirit, he was going to Jerusalem, not knowing what would happen, except that prison and hardships were waiting. "However, I consider my life worth nothing to me; my only aim is to finish the race and complete the task the Lord Jesus has given me: testifying to the good news of God's grace." They would not see him again. He urged them, "Keep watch over yourselves and all the flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the church of God." Savage wolves would come, even from among them. He committed them to God and to the word of his grace. He had not wanted anyone's silver or gold, but worked to support himself and others, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus: "It is more blessed to give than to receive." He knelt and prayed with them all. They wept as they embraced him, grieved most that they would never see his face again. Then they went with him to the ship.

summary.bigIdea: Paul says a tearful goodbye to the church leaders of Ephesus, determined to finish the task Jesus gave him.
points: On Sunday at Troas, Eutychus falls from a window and is brought back to life.
Paul tells the Ephesian elders to shepherd God's church faithfully.
"It is more blessed to give than to receive."
summary.reflection: Paul wanted to "finish the race" well. What would finishing well look like in your life?
